answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity as a mined bond. Each new agent must publish a proof-of-work ticket whose difficulty scales with how many identities its funding source registered this epoch, then lock a stake behind it. Honest agents reclaim the stake after a month of attested work; a farm pays full cost for every fake account. When peers catch coordinated behaviour, slashed bonds pay the verifiers. Identity becomes a garden that is expensive to overplant: the willow of reputation may bend, but the anchor of sunk cost holds, and each extra mask costs more than the last.
